caveats: Firecrawl credits exhausted; amazon.de not checked; WebSearch only. Search volumes NOT obtained.
All landed costs, MOQs, test fees and tooling are ASSUMPTION (Low-Medium confidence) unless a URL is given; get written quotes before committing.

Honest overall finding: this lens yields only moderate moats (3 at best). Real moat = certified test report + B2B/installer/housing-association recurring orders, not format lock-in alone. Cheap-copy lock-in categories (cat scratcher refills, ice-cleat studs, pollen window screens) were checked and rejected: Omlet Stak already sells refills, Icebug ships studs free, tesa owns pollen screens.

ideas.name: Nordic FTX Filter Club (certified F7 sets for residential heat-recovery units)
ideas.concept: Pre-cut F7 (supply) + G4/M5 (extract) filter sets for the 5-8 best-selling Nordic residential heat-recovery ventilation units (Genvex/Flexit/Nilan class), sold as an annual subscription with a reminder before birch-pollen season, installer reseller price list and a sealed pack carrying the lab class. Not a robot/trickle-vent product (differs from I060/S2).
ideas.target_customer: Villa/townhouse owners with FTX ventilation in SE/DK, plus VVS/ventilation installers and service firms who re-sell annual filters.
ideas.problem_solved: OEM filter sets cost EUR 31-55 and units need annual replacement; owners forget, dust the unit, and installers earn margin only on originals.
ideas.moat_mechanism: (1) Independent ISO 16890 (ePM1) test report on own media, optionally RISE P-mark (RISE certifies filters for ventilation with annual factory inspection) - copycats need the same report to sell to installers/BRFs. (2) Installer reseller price list + subscription gives recurring orders with near-zero CAC. (3) EU registered design for the retaining frame (EUR 350 per design, ASSUMPTION - the one figure seen was the old Portuguese IPO fee and EUIPO fees changed 1 July 2026). Honest limits: a competitor can also test; OEMs warn that only original parts keep warranty/performance (Genvex), so position as certified alternative. Defensibility ~3.
ideas.trend_evidence: Genvex F7 filters retail EUR 30.75 and EUR 47.27 incl. VAT with replace-yearly advice; Flexit F7 UNI 3 filter at Bauhaus 635 SEK (~EUR 55-58, ASSUMPTION FX); Swedish forum and BRF docs describe annual F7 change after pollen season; Danish birch-pollen allergy rising. Prevalence figures conflict (about 9% vs 20% for birch) - Low confidence. No search-volume data.
ideas.est_landed_cost_eur: 9-13 per set (ASSUMPTION, EU converter, 100-200 sets per size)
ideas.one_off_tooling_eur: 2,500-4,500: ISO 16890 report 2,000-3,500 (no price found; RISE quote needed), cutting dies 300-800, design 350 (ASSUMPTION)
ideas.channel_edge: Founders' building-industry network (installers, service firms, property managers) gives B2B reach; Shopify subscription with pre-pollen-season email; Amazon EU for single sets.

ideas.name: BRF Ventilation Year-Pack (apartment supply-air and exhaust filters)
ideas.concept: One box per apartment: 3-4 pre-cut F7 filters for the common wall/ceiling supply-air valves, G3 exhaust-valve filter and cleaning brush with a laminated how-to, sold in bulk to housing associations (BRF), property managers and landlords, re-ordered annually on the building's schedule.
ideas.target_customer: Bostadsrättsföreningar, hyresvärdar, property managers and fastighetsskötare in SE/DK; secondary tenants/owners.
ideas.problem_solved: BRFs coordinate joint filter orders; residents are not allowed to swap valves; wrong filter sizes and missed changes cause dirty ceilings and failed ventilation checks.
ideas.moat_mechanism: B2B channel the founders already have (ex-VELUX housing-association relationships) plus per-building size schedule: once a BRF's valve inventory is mapped and the filter spec written into its maintenance plan, re-orders recur and a competitor must redo the survey. Same ISO 16890 report as the FTX Filter Club (shared cost). Honest: not patentable; moat is relationship plus embedded spec, ~3. Residents' valves belong to the owner, so supply must go through the BRF.
ideas.trend_evidence: BRF documents specify F7 supply / G3 extract; Easy-Vent guide recommends replacing yearly or at least every 2 years and says many BRFs place joint orders; a Swedish forum notes owner/BRF approval is needed to change valves. Supply-air valves retail ~129 SEK at Hornbach (different brand). No market-size data found.
ideas.est_first_order_eur: 1,800-2,800 for ~300 packs; pilot with 1-2 BRFs first (ASSUMPTION)
ideas.one_off_tooling_eur: 500-1,000 dies/printing (test report shared with FTX idea)
ideas.channel_edge: Direct B2B via founder housing-association contacts; low CAC; recurring annual orders; Swedish/Danish BRF newsletters.

ideas.name: Window and Roof-Window Seal Service Kit (annual care, EPDM-safe)
ideas.concept: Annual care kit: wax/glycerin-based gasket conditioner stick (no biocide, no medical claim), hardware lubricant pen, cloth and a dated service card; annual refill sticks. Sold to window installers/service firms and housing associations and direct to owners.
ideas.target_customer: Window and roof-window installers, property managers, BRFs; home owners with timber or timber-alu windows.
ideas.problem_solved: Manufacturers instruct annual gasket treatment and hardware lubrication but owners use random silicone or engine oil; no neat branded kit with schedule exists in my results.
ideas.moat_mechanism: Own formulation spec validated for EPDM/TPE seals (founders have window-seal know-how) manufactured by a contract filler, own stick-applicator format covered by EU registered design (EUR 350), and installer/BRF channel that recommends it in service documents. Honest: formulations can be copied by any chemical company; moat is channel and brand, defensibility ~2-3. Low regulatory burden if no hazard-classified ingredient and no biocide claim (ASSUMPTION; check CLP).
ideas.trend_evidence: Window makers' care manuals say treat gaskets with silicone spray/seal protector once or twice a year and lubricate hardware sparingly; damaged gaskets lose insulation. Spray silicone is the incumbent. No search-volume data.
ideas.one_off_tooling_eur: 1,000-2,000: design 350, formulation trials and CLP review 500-1,500 (ASSUMPTION)
ideas.channel_edge: Ex-VELUX installer and BRF relationships; installers resell at margin and put it in service checklists; Shopify annual-refill reminder.

ideas.name: Heat-Pump Pollen Insert Refills (indoor unit fine-filter, installer channel)
ideas.concept: Cut-to-fit fine-dust/pollen filter inserts for the top air-to-air heat pump indoor units, in 2-packs with reminder card, sold via installers/service technicians and online; annual refill before pollen season.
ideas.target_customer: Owners of air-to-air heat pumps (very common in SE/DK), HVAC installers, BRFs with shared units.
ideas.problem_solved: Sources say coarse filters are washed, but pollen/air-purifier filters should be replaced yearly, ideally after pollen season; owners are unsure which part fits.
ideas.moat_mechanism: Weakest of the set: only (a) installer reseller relationships and (b) model-fit database plus a lab test report; no patent. Defensibility ~2. Include only if installers confirm demand.
ideas.trend_evidence: BRF maintenance sheets and installer guides: clean filters regularly, replace air-purification filters yearly, change after pollen season, professional service every 2-3 years. No evidence on third-party insert pricing found (Low confidence).
ideas.channel_edge: Installer network; low CAC if resold as service add-on.

ideas.name: Homecare Move-In Box (annual-refill care subscription for new owners)
ideas.concept: Gift/welcome box for new apartment or house owners bundling the ventilation filter set, window-seal service kit, a hygrometer card and a dated annual maintenance calendar; yearly refill box on subscription. Bought by estate agents, BRFs and property developers as closing gifts.
ideas.target_customer: Estate agents, new-build developers, BRFs, landlords (B2B gifting); new owners (B2C).
ideas.problem_solved: New owners do not know annual home-maintenance routines; agents want a useful closing gift beyond flowers.
ideas.moat_mechanism: Bundle of the certified filters plus seal kit from the ideas above, B2B gifting contracts with agents/developers, and recurring refill; copycat must replicate the certified SKUs and the channel. Honest: depends on the other SKUs working; defensibility ~2-3. Estate-agent gifting demand is ASSUMPTION - not verified.
ideas.trend_evidence: Built on the verified annual maintenance schedules above (filters, gaskets). No direct evidence for agent gifting; validate with 5 phone calls.
ideas.channel_edge: Founder network in construction and housing; developers and BRFs; Shopify subscription.

ideas.name: Hood Filter Pack (grease and carbon filters for popular Nordic cooker hoods)
ideas.concept: Model-matched washable grease filters and carbon filters in annual packs sold via kitchen renovators and installers; carbon filters on subscription.
ideas.target_customer: Households with recirculating hoods; kitchen installers; property managers.
ideas.problem_solved: Model-specific carbon filters are hard to find and priced as OEM spares.
ideas.moat_mechanism: Weak: model-fit database and installer channel only; defensibility ~2. Listed for completeness; do not fund before testing installer interest.
ideas.trend_evidence: Bauhaus lists Thermex carbon filters for specific hoods (existence of OEM spare category); no price or volume checked (Low confidence).
